title: schema negotiation: bidirectional response_format + OpenAI-compat error mapping
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Customers building strict structured-output pipelines need predictable behavior when models stream partial tokens, when clients ask for OpenAI-compatible error codes, and when function-calling instruments interact with response_format negotiation. This PR implements bidirectional schema negotiation (client-specified response_format + runtime-augmented hints), a compact error-code mapping layer for OpenAI-compat consumers, and stream-recovery signals so callers can decide whether to retry or fallback.

What this changes at a high level: 1) ResponseFormatNegotiator: a small runtime component that takes the user-supplied response_format (json_schema, text, openai_compat) and the model capability profile and selects a streaming/strictness strategy. 2) StrictMode Opt-in Flag: new request parameter response_format.strict (opt-in) that enables hard schema validation on complete and streaming mode; violations are surfaced as structured errors rather than free-text warnings. 3) Stream Recovery Header: during streaming, when an invalid JSON chunk or schema violation is detected, the runtime emits a small control event (EVENT: schema_error) with a canonical error code and a short token cursor so clients can choose to rewind/skip or fallback to a non-strict route. 4) OpenAI-compat error mapping: new compact mapper that translates internal schema error classes to OpenAI-compatible error categories (e.g., invalid_request_error -> invalid_response_format, resource_exhausted -> model_capacity) and preserves guidance text. 5) Function-calling interplay: the negotiator now marks function call envelopes as tolerant by default unless response_format.strict=true. This avoids hard failures in common function-calling workflows while allowing strict validation for verification flows.

Changes included (summary): commits: add negotiator, add strict flag parsing in API surface, stream event plumbing, error mapper and tests, docs update, TS SDK typing for response_format, Python SDK acceptance tests, small perf tweak to streaming parser to keep latency within SLO.

Compatibility notes: - Default behavior unchanged for existing clients (strict=false by default). - OpenAI-compat explicit mode maps legacy error shapes; behavior only activates if client requests openai_compat or sets compatibility headers. - Private/Dedicated customers can pin default strictness via account config (follow-up PR in dedicated config).

Testing and rollout: unit + integration coverage added for negotiation permutations (json_schema streaming/non-streaming, text, openai_compat). End-to-end canary on perf-canary for 24h with rollback flag. Feature gated behind runtime flag `negotiator_v2` and released via canary->gradual->global rollout.

Follow-ups: - Dedicated: expose account-level default strictness and an importable policy bundle. - Observability: surfaced metric redwood.response_format.violation.count and histogram of recovery latency. - SDK ergonomics: add high-level helper to auto-handle schema_error events.

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-2024, ENG-2121, SUP-891.
